title: Joe Keyes's decline and death
summary: Keyes later became an alcoholic and was found dead in the Hudson; Clayton also recalls seeing him in Parsons in a Texas band.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well now, I've been told that he, well he was an alcoholic or was that later?
Later he was.
Not at that time?

He didn't touch a drop. He's like Elman Ziggy. When he was with Benny he was the only one that wouldn't drink. It used to be, get after Harry and Chris Griffin. Sometimes they would get drunk, but he wouldn't touch it.
He died an alcoholic. And Jo was always the neatest one in the band, or one of the neatest. Herschel I think was about the neatest one.
: Herschel was?
Yes. Herschel always looked like a real dignified lawyer or..... Beautifully dressed. He wouldn't go out that everything was in, everything was in line before he would go out.

And Joe eventually got to, after he left Basie, he went with Bill Robinson. Bill Robinson liked him, bought him a new trumpet. But by that time he was on, drinking wine, he was a wino, in the Braddock Hotel.

So he got to hanging out with these guys that were drinking to death. Everytime he'd get some money they'd drink it up. And he got worse and worse until he was finally sleeping in the street. So he sent home to Texas and his mother sent him something like two hundred dollars. So he lets, buys all these cronies drinks and wine. Everybody knew he had some money.
And the next day they found him in the Hudson River with a big gash in his head. Somebody
had done that to him to get that little money he had. And that was the end of it.
Do you suggest by that though that the reason he was a bit of our tune was because of it?
I think so. I always figured that. It's hard to blow a horn out of tune if it's a good horn.
But he was a schooled musician then, well trained?

Yes. When I was in Parsons. I remember Joe Keyes coming through my home when I was still in school. You know, like every now and then they had a dance in a park in my home. It was called Forest Park. And I remember seeing Joe Keyes. I'd make all the dances and I never would dance, I'd just go there and look at the band and listen to the band. Never would dance.
And I remember seeing Joe Keyes. But he was in a Texas band then. The band that he, was coming out of Texas. Probably went on to Kansas City.
Was he in Moten's band?
Joe Keyes?
I don't think so.
Oh.
